validity.recommendation: sheet wrong — set LengthKnown (=LengthKnownKm)=240 (km), not 310. The sheet's 310km/Damietta figure reflects the ORIGINAL 2018 proposal (Egypt Petroleum Minister/Cyprus Energy Minister MoU, Damietta Segas LNG terminal endpoint). That plan was superseded: the Feb 2025 Cypriot-government-approved Development and Production Plan (DPP) re-routes the export line to a shorter subsea tie-back landing at Port Said, not Damietta. Three independent, non-GEM sources (MEES trade press, Washington Institute think-tank, Arab Center DC think-tank) each report the current design as a ~240km/150-mile pipeline to Port Said — consistent with the drawn-route geodesic measurement of 215km (ratio 215/240=0.90, inside the 0.75–1.33 allowed band; the sheet's old 310km value gives 215/310=0.69, outside it). This resolves the flag as a stale LENGTH VALUE, not a wrong/partial drawn route — the drawn route is actually closer to the current reality than the sheet's own length figure is. Note (out of scope for this flag, flagging for a separate pass): EndLocation/EndState currently reads 'Damietta Segas LNG Terminal' / 'Damietta', which is also now stale per the same Port Said re-route — an EndLocation correction would likely also warrant a routes-repo geometry PR, but that is a distinct fix from the length value requested here.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked: (1) MEES (Middle East Economic Survey, subscription trade press, 21 Feb 2025) — explicit quote: 'a 17 February MoU that would see all Aphrodite output piped from an above-field floating production unit (FPU) to Egypt via a 240km tie-back to Port Said.' (2) Washington Institute policy analysis — 'the solution—as proposed by a consortium with production rights led by Chevron—is to pump the gas southward to Egypt via a shorter 150-mile seabed pipeline' (150mi=241.4km, consistent with MEES's 240km). (3) Arab Center DC — 'Chevron has proposed a production plan involving what it describes as a cost-effective 150-mile tieback pipeline to Port Said in Egypt, which was approved in February 2025.' All three are independent origins (specialist O&G trade press + two separate US think tanks), none reprints another, none cites GEM. Also confirmed via Rigzone (10 Apr 2026, on the April 2026 EGAS supply-term-sheet) that 'the final delivery point shall be determined at the metering station at the onshore terminal in Port Said, Egypt' — corroborating the Port Said (not Damietta) endpoint independently of the length figure. Did not find any 2025/2026-era source still citing 310km or Damietta as current — those figures only appear in 2018-vintage coverage and in GEM's own wiki mirror of the sheet (not used as evidence). Currently 'Length [ref]' on the sheet is blank (orphan value with no ref) — this fill also closes that gap.
